state_program_name: Home Services Agency license (IDPH) under the Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Licensing Act (210 ILCS 55; 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245). Non-medical in-home services paid privately, or through the IDoA Community Care Program and the DHS-DRS Home Services Program.

front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** delivers non-medical in-home services in Illinois in compliance with the Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Licensing Act (210 ILCS 55) and the Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Code (77 Ill. Adm. Code 245). It supports [AGENCY NAME]'s Home Services Agency license from the Illinois Department of Public Health (IDPH). It covers services paid privately and services paid through the IDoA Community Care Program and the DHS-DRS Home Services Program.

The manual is written to:

- Give staff, supervisors, and the governing body one written source for how the agency operates, as 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30 requires of written administrative and personnel policies.
- Keep services within the non-medical scope that Part 245 allows. Home services means help with activities of daily living, housekeeping, personal laundry, and companionship. It excludes anything that requires a Nurse Practice Act licensee.
- Protect clients' safety, dignity, privacy, and rights.
- Help the agency prepare for IDPH licensure review and compliance surveys.

**Service model.** Part 245 treats a direct-service (employer) home services agency differently from a home services *placement* agency. A placement agency may not be the employer, may not direct or supervise workers, and may charge only a one-time placement fee. **[AGENCY NAME] must state in this manual which model it uses: [DIRECT-SERVICE AGENCY / PLACEMENT AGENCY].** Sections that apply to only one model are marked as such.

**Scope note.** Under 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.20, a program that serves clients *exclusively* through the IDoA Community Care Program, the DHS Office of Rehabilitation Services, or the VA is not a home services agency. [AGENCY NAME] should confirm its licensure status against its actual payer mix before adopting this manual. IDPH-licensed agencies take private pay or private insurance. Medicaid-funded clients are served through IDoA CCP or DHS-DRS.

**This manual is a template.** It must be customized for [AGENCY NAME] and does not replace the Act, the Code, or advice from qualified legal or compliance counsel.
front_matter.how_to_use:
## How to Use This Manual

### 1. Customize it before use
This manual contains placeholders such as **[AGENCY NAME]**, **[AGENCY MANAGER]**, **[ALTERNATE AGENCY MANAGER]**, **[ADDRESS]**, and **[PHONE]**. Replace every placeholder with agency-specific information. Revise the procedures so they match what [AGENCY NAME] actually does: its service model, counties served, payers, staffing, operating hours, forms, and systems. Do not leave in any policy the agency does not follow. A written policy that is not followed is a compliance risk.

### 2. Adopt it through the governing body
Under 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(a), the governing body must adopt and revise the agency's operating policies and procedures, meet to review agency operations, and keep minutes of all meetings. Record formal adoption of this manual, and of each later revision, in the governing body's minutes. Record the adoption date and version on the cover page.

### 3. Keep it current
- Assign one person, such as the agency manager, to own the manual and track changes.
- Review the whole manual at least annually, and sooner when a rule, payer requirement, or agency practice changes. The governing body's bylaws must also be reviewed annually (245.30(a)).
- Check the current text of 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245 and 210 ILCS 55 on the Illinois General Assembly and JCAR websites. Part 245 was most recently amended at 49 Ill. Reg. 4661, eff. 3/25/2025, and may change again.
- Keep a revision log showing the date, section changed, reason, and who approved it.
- Notify IDPH of agency changes within 10 days, using the Facility Information Change Form. The agency also needs IDPH approval before serving a new county.

### 4. Train staff on it
Every employee, and every contracted worker who provides services for the agency, must be oriented to the manual and trained on the parts that apply to their role. Part 245 requires orientation and continuing education (245.30(c)(1)(C)), and the agency manager must familiarize employees with the Act and rules (245.40(a)). Keep the Department's rules on file at the agency (245.40(a)). Document each training with the date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content, and worker signature or dated electronic certificate (245.71(i)). Keep a signed acknowledgment from each staff member that they have received and read the manual and its updates.

### 5. Verify items flagged for full-text review
The research behind this template could not confirm the full text of some provisions. Before finalizing, read the current rule text for the following and complete the procedure from it:

- 245.40(c)(4)(M)-(P), the remaining acceptable tasks and limitations after toileting.
- 245.40(c)(6)(B), the routine supervisory-visit interval. Do not rely on secondary-source figures.
- 245.40(c)(4)(N) and (c)(5)(D), the exact wording on medication reminding and the prohibition on medication setup.
- 245.75(b), the infection control subsection on adherence to CDC guidance.
- 245.240(a)-(b), the content of the annual quality improvement evaluation and record review.
- 245.90(a), the minimum liability insurance limits. Do not rely on secondary-source figures.

### 6. Organization
Citations in the body of the manual point to the specific Part 245 section that supports each policy, so staff and surveyors can trace a policy to its source. Statements marked as survey guidance or program requirements (for example IDPH guidance, EVV, or payer rules) are not rules in Part 245 and should be read as such.
front_matter.regulatory_framework:
## Regulatory Framework

The rules below are the sources this manual relies on, listed by their cite text. Check the current official text of each before relying on it.

### A. Licensure statute and code
- **210 ILCS 55**, Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Licensing Act. No one may open, manage, conduct, or maintain a home services agency without an IDPH license. It is the enabling statute for Part 245.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245**, Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Code. It has four subparts: A General (245.10-245.25), B Operational Requirements (245.30-245.75), C Licensure Procedures (245.80-245.150), and D Client/Patient Services (245.200-245.250).
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.20**, Definitions. This includes the definition of "client record" and the exclusion of programs serving clients exclusively through IDoA CCP, DHS Office of Rehabilitation Services, or the VA.

### B. Organization, administration, and personnel
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(a)**, governing body, bylaws, adoption of policies, and meeting minutes.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(b)(1)-(3)**, written administrative policies, evidence of liability insurance, and complaint-resolution policies.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(c)(1)(A)-(I)**, written personnel policies.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(c)(2)-(5)**, license verification with IDFPR, personnel records, and contracted staff.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.30(f)(1)**, designation of a person to supervise services (agency manager).
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.40(a)(1)-(13)**, agency manager responsibilities, including the office, telephone, confidentiality, backup designee, and operating-hours policy.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.90(a)**, evidence of liability insurance.

### C. Worker scope, supervision, qualifications, and training
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.40(c)(1)-(3)**, home services worker definition and duties.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.40(c)(4)(A)-(L)**, acceptable tasks and limitations, skin care through toileting. Items (M)-(P) must be read in full.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.40(c)(4)(N); 245.40(c)(5)(D)**, medication reminding and the prohibition on medication setup.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.40(c)(6)**, supervision of home services workers.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.71(a)**, employment conditions and file documentation.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.71(c)**, initial training (at least 10 hours, with competency evaluations).
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.71(e)(1)-(14)**, required training subjects.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.71(f)**, annual training (at least 10 hours per year).
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.71(g)-(i)**, supervisor/trainer qualifications and training documentation.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.72**, Health Care Worker Background Check.
- **225 ILCS 46; 77 Ill. Adm. Code 955**, Health Care Worker Background Check Act and Code.

### D. Client services and safety
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.210(a)-(b)**, scope of home services, list of services, and contracted services.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.210(c)**, written client agreement.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.210(d)**, acceptance of clients and discharge.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.210(e)-(g)**, service plan.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.210(h)-(j)**, client records, retention, and confidentiality.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.75(a)**, infection control.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.240(a)**, quality improvement program.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.250**, abuse, neglect, and financial exploitation prevention and reporting. Mandated-reporter duties under **320 ILCS 20** (Adult Protective Services Act) remain in force.

### E. Licensing procedure
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.100**, provisional license.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.130(b)**, adverse licensure actions, including an application not completed within 90 days.

### F. Provisions that apply to only some agencies
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.214**, Home Services *Placement* Agency. It does not apply to a direct-service (employer) agency.
- **77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.55(a)**, vaccinations. The influenza and pneumococcal duties apply to home health and home nursing agencies, not to home services agencies. This manual does not include client vaccination procedures.

### G. Guidance and program requirements (not Part 245 rules)
- **IDPH Home Services Agencies FAQ**, covering the application review, compliance survey timing, county expansion, and change notices.
- **IDPH Guidance for Common Deficiency Findings**, which covers annual Health Care Worker Registry verification and annual education. It is survey guidance, not a rule.
- **IDPH Home Services Application, Form 445104**, which lists the policies and documents that must accompany the application, including proof of IDPH Registry access.
- **HFS Electronic Visit Verification; December 2025 Illinois EVV Updates**, for Medicaid personal care.
- **IDoA Community Care Program current rates (eff. 1/1/2026)**, **DHS-DRS Home Services Program rates (updated 7/1/2026)**, and **HFS Persons who are Elderly waiver**, which apply when serving publicly funded clients.

### Regulators and Contact Information

| Agency | Role | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **Illinois Department of Public Health (IDPH), Home Services Program** | Licenses home services agencies: initial application, provisional license, surveys, county-expansion approval, change notices. | Phone: 217-782-7412 (TTY 800-547-0466). Email: DPH.COOS@illinois.gov. Web: https://dph.illinois.gov/topics-services/health-care-regulation/health-care-facilities/home-services.html |
| **Illinois Department on Aging (IDoA), Community Care Program** | Operating agency for the Persons who are Elderly HCBS waiver. Sets CCP in-home rates. Care Coordination Units assess and refer clients. | Senior HelpLine: 1-800-252-8966. Web: https://ilaging.illinois.gov/programs/ccp/current-rates.html |
| **Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS)** | State Medicaid agency. HCBS waiver oversight and Electronic Visit Verification policy. | Web: https://hfs.illinois.gov/medicalclients/hcbs/elderly.html. [AGENCY NAME] to add the current phone/email. |
| **Illinois Department of Human Services, Division of Rehabilitation Services (DHS-DRS)** | Home Services Program for people with severe disabilities under age 60. Sets HSP maximum unit prices. | Web: https://www.dhs.state.il.us/page.aspx?item=67182. [AGENCY NAME] to add the current phone/email. |

Other agencies named in the rules cited above are the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (IDFPR), for license verification; the Illinois State Police, for fingerprint-based background checks; the IDoA-designated elder abuse provider agency or Area Agency on Aging; the DCFS Child Abuse Hotline; and local police or 911. [AGENCY NAME] should insert current contact numbers for these in its abuse-reporting and emergency procedures.

### Keeping this section accurate
Rules and contacts change. The governing body and agency manager must confirm the current text of each cited rule and the current contact details for each regulator at every annual review, and must update this section whenever a rule or contact changes.

citations.title: Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Licensing Act
citations.requirement: No one may open, manage, conduct or maintain a home services agency without an IDPH license. The Act is the enabling statute for 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245. (From the fact-checked research; Act text not re-fetched.)

citations.title: Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Code
citations.requirement: Part 245 has four subparts: A General (245.10-245.25), B Operational Requirements (245.30-245.75), C Licensure Procedures (245.80-245.150), D Client/Patient Services (245.200-245.250). Section titles were confirmed from the table of contents. Most recent amendment shown: 49 Ill. Reg. 4661, eff. 3/25/2025.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Programs serving clients exclusively through IDoA CCP, DHS Office of Rehabilitation Services, or the VA are not home services agencies. 'Client record' means personal information, emergency notification information, agreed service plans, the home services contract, and documentation of services at each visit.

citations.title: Organization and Administration - Governing Body (all agencies)
citations.requirement: The agency must have a governing body with legal authority. The body must have bylaws or the equivalent, reviewed annually and revised as needed, that state the agency's objectives. It must adopt and revise operating policies and procedures, meet to review agency operations, and keep minutes of all meetings. The requirement to employ a qualified administrator is for home health agencies.

citations.title: Administration - all agencies
citations.requirement: The agency needs written administrative policies and procedures to ensure safe and adequate care. It must show evidence of liability insurance per 245.90(a). It must have written complaint-resolution policies between the agency and its clients and client advocates.

citations.title: Personnel policies - all agencies
citations.requirement: Written personnel policies must cover: (A) wage scales, benefits, hours and leave; (B) initial health evaluation of each new employee with client contact; (C) orientation and continuing education; (D) job descriptions for all positions; (E) annual performance evaluation; (F) Civil Rights Act of 1964 compliance; (G) confidentiality of personnel records; (H) employee health policy, including symptom and exposure reporting and removal from and return to client contact; (I) procedures for identifying and protecting staff from dangers in the home.

citations.title: Personnel - license verification, personnel records, contracted staff
citations.requirement: Before employing anyone in a position needing a State professional license, verify with IDFPR that the license is active and keep a copy in the personnel file. Personnel records must hold name and address, SSN, date of birth, next of kin, evidence of qualifications, employment dates, and the reason for separation. Home services agencies that use contracted services must ensure those workers hold any required license, registration or certification and are supervised by the agency.

citations.title: Agency Manager - Home Services and Home Nursing Agencies
citations.requirement: A home services agency must designate a person to supervise the provision of services (or oversee placement of workers). This is the verified designation rule. The research's reference to '245.40(f)' could not be confirmed and should not be used. No manager qualification list for home services agencies appears in 245.30(f) as fetched.

citations.title: Staffing - Administrator or Agency Manager responsibilities
citations.requirement: The manager must ensure legal compliance, know the Department's rules, keep them in the agency, and familiarize employees with the Act and rules. The manager keeps reports, records, personnel files and policies, maintains an organizational chart, hires per job descriptions, and provides orientation and in-service education. The manager must designate in writing a qualified person to act in the manager's absence. The agency must keep an office with a working telephone staffed during business hours. The office must protect record confidentiality and comply with fire-safety ordinances. The agency must adopt a written operating-hours policy that tells clients how to access care outside those hours.

citations.title: Home Services or In-Home Services Worker - definition and duties
citations.requirement: Home services means help with ADLs, housekeeping, personal laundry and companionship in the client's residence. It excludes anything requiring a Nurse Practice Act licensee. Workers may observe and report changes in client functioning, do chores and meal preparation, help with shopping and appointments, provide companionship, document services, and assist with ADLs and personal care. Workers provide services only as Part 245 allows.

citations.title: Acceptable tasks and limitations (skin care through toileting)
citations.requirement: Task-by-task limits apply for skin care, ambulation, bathing, dressing/compression, exercise, feeding/thickener, hair care, mouth care, nail care, positioning, shaving and toileting. Most require three things: client or representative feedback, worker training in the method, and an agency competency evaluation. Several also require a health care professional's order. No passive range of motion, no nail trimming, and no skilled skin care. The fetched page was truncated after toileting (L), so the remaining items (M-P) must be read in full.

citations.title: Medication reminding; prohibited medication setup
citations.requirement: A worker may remind a client about medications only when they were pre-selected by the client, a family member, a nurse or a pharmacist and are in containers other than prescription bottles, such as medication minders. A worker may not perform or provide medication setup. Source: ilga.gov excerpts and the Illinois Register adoption text, seen in search results. Confirm the exact subsection wording in the full text.

citations.title: Supervision of a home services worker
citations.requirement: A supervisor must be designated and available to workers for questions at all times (not applicable to placement agencies). Supervisory visits must include an on-site visit within the next supervisory visit when an area of concern is noted. The supervisor must also make an annual on-site visit to observe and assess each worker giving care. The visit interval for routine supervision is not confirmed. A secondary source says 90 days; read the full text of (c)(6)(B) before publishing.

citations.title: Qualifications and Requirements for Home Services Workers - employment conditions
citations.requirement: For each worker who is not otherwise licensed, certified or registered, the agency must keep in the employee file documentation of: (1) no disqualifying Health Care Worker Background Check without a waiver; (2) a copy of the Social Security card; (3) a visa or proof of citizenship that meets federal employment requirements.

citations.title: Initial training - home services agency
citations.requirement: The agency must provide or arrange at least 10 hours of initial training per worker. Five hours must come before the first assignment, and the other 5 within 30 days of the start of employment. The agency may accept proof of training from another licensed home services agency within the prior 365 days, including a CNA on the Health Care Worker Registry. Such workers still get a competency evaluation before their first assignment. No assignment may be given until the worker passes a competency evaluation on the first 5 hours of topics, with a second test after the remaining 5 hours. (The 8-hour figure in 245.71(b) and 245.214(e) applies only to placement agencies.)

citations.title: Required training subjects
citations.requirement: Training must cover, in addition to 245.40(c)(4)(A)-(P): job responsibilities and limits; communication with people who are hard of hearing or have dementia; observing, reporting and documenting; personal care tasks including medication reminding; adaptive equipment; hygiene and infection control; a clean and safe environment; safety precautions; emergencies, first aid and the client's emergency preparedness plan; confidentiality; understanding dementia; problem-solving for challenging dementia behaviors; abuse and neglect and reporting duties; and any other task the agency assigns.

citations.title: Annual training
citations.requirement: Every worker needs at least 10 hours of training per year of employment, on a calendar-year or anniversary basis chosen by the agency. The initial 10 hours satisfy the first year. Self-study with demonstrated learning is allowed. Annual training must include: client dignity, independence, self-determination, privacy, choice and rights; disaster procedures; hygiene and infection control; abuse and neglect prevention and reporting; and the ADL tasks in 245.40(c)(4)(A)-(P), including oxygen delivery for workers who serve clients on oxygen.

citations.title: Supervisors/trainers and training documentation
citations.requirement: The agency must have home services supervisors or trainers who give initial training and ongoing supervision. Each must either (1) have at least 2 years of qualifying experience within the last 5 years, or (2) hold a current supervisory or trainer position and have had training within the past year on the permitted tasks, provided by or developed by a qualified professional. Supervisors and trainers must be available to workers for continuing education. All training must be documented with date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content description, and worker signature or electronic certificate with date/time stamp.

citations.title: Health Care Worker Background Check
citations.requirement: An agency must comply with the Health Care Worker Background Check Act (225 ILCS 46) and the Health Care Worker Background Check Code (77 Ill. Adm. Code 955).

citations.title: Health Care Worker Background Check Act and Code
citations.requirement: Fingerprint-based checks are required for covered workers. Fingerprints are sent to the Illinois State Police within 10 working days (per the research). Results initiated through IDPH are entered in the Health Care Worker Registry. The application package requires proof of access to the IDPH Registry (955.115, per Form 445104).

citations.title: Infection Control
citations.requirement: Each agency must develop and implement policies and procedures for investigating, controlling and preventing infections. The requirement for placement agencies to give workers the CDC hand-hygiene guideline does not apply to a direct-service agency. Subsection (b), on adherence to CDC guidance, was only partly visible; read it in full.

citations.title: Vaccinations (scope)
citations.requirement: Influenza and pneumococcal vaccination duties apply to home health agencies and home nursing agencies, not to home services agencies. Do not write client vaccination procedures for this license.

citations.title: Services - Home Services Agencies: scope and contracted services
citations.requirement: A home services agency provides non-medical services, directly or by contract, such as ADL support, personal care, medication reminding, housekeeping, laundry, cooking, shopping, transport to appointments, household records and companionship. The agency must keep a list of services offered and the scope of work for each. It must give that list to clients before contracting, with the signed contract, and whenever it changes. Contracts with third-party providers must be written and include 9 elements: services, adherence to agency policies and personnel requirements, agency control, notes, charges, liability and insurance, term, signatures, and termination.

citations.title: Written client agreement
citations.requirement: A written client agreement must include: (1) assurance of compliance with the Act, including the Health Care Worker Background Check Act; (2) who pays employment taxes, Social Security taxes and workers' compensation; (3) who supervises workers and who hires, fires and disciplines them; (4) charges, payment schedule and payee; (5) contract term and termination conditions; (6) contact information for concerns, complaints and questions.

citations.title: Acceptance of clients; discharge
citations.requirement: The agency must develop and follow written acceptance and discharge policies. Acceptance is based on need for non-medical help, and the agency may not provide medical services. A totally dependent repositioning client may be accepted only if the worker is trained and competency-evaluated and the representative can assist or give feedback. No one may be refused service on the basis of the protected classes listed in 775 ILCS 5/1-103(Q). Termination requires at least 7 working days' written notice with a stated reason, kept in the record. The 7-day notice does not apply when worker safety is at risk, and the risk must be documented. Acceptance must be based on documented functional limitations and relevant circumstances, including basic information on medications, treatments, activity, diet and mental status.

citations.title: Service plan
citations.requirement: A plan is required for every client, developed with agency staff, the client or representative or POA, and family if the client wishes. It must cover ADL and in-home support, medication reminders (frequency and time of day), treatments being received, activity, diet, functional limitations and essential procedures, mental health status, frequency of visits, equipment, and client limitations. It may not include tasks outside the worker scope in 245.40(c)(4). No physician signature is required. Review and revise as needed, and at least annually.

citations.title: Client records, retention, confidentiality
citations.requirement: Each client record must hold identifying information, representative contact information, an emergency contact, the agreed service plan, the signed home care services agreement, and worker documentation of each service at each visit. A written records policy is required. Records must be kept at least 2 years after the last date of service, in hard copy or electronic form. Faxed copies must be on non-thermal paper. A written confidentiality policy must cover use, removal and release of records.

citations.title: Quality Improvement Program
citations.requirement: Home nursing, home services and placement agencies must develop a quality improvement program with written policies. The program must evaluate the agency's total program at least once a year. Subsection (b) requires record review. Its detail, and the content of the evaluation for home services agencies, was not retrieved; read in full.

citations.title: Abuse, Neglect and Financial Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
citations.requirement: On reasonable suspicion of abuse, neglect or financial exploitation of a client aged 60+, a disabled client, or any 'eligible adult' under the Adult Protective Services Act (320 ILCS 20), notify the elder abuse provider agency designated by IDoA or the Area Agency on Aging. For a victim under 18, call the DCFS Child Abuse Hotline. Document each report and keep it on premises for 12 months. If an employee is the alleged perpetrator, remove them from direct client contact immediately and investigate. Complete a written investigation report within 14 days of the initial report. Send it to IDPH within 24 hours after the investigation is completed and keep a copy for 12 months. The report must contain the six elements in (d). Employees and volunteers must report to management and to the elder abuse provider agency or IDoA. Call 911 or local police immediately for staff-inflicted physical injury, sexual abuse by staff, a crime in the home by another person, or a death other than by disease or natural causes. A written law-enforcement notification policy is required. Mandated-reporter duties under 320 ILCS 20 remain.

citations.title: Services - Home Services Placement Agency
citations.requirement: A placement agency may not be the employer, may not direct or supervise the worker, and may charge only a one-time placement fee. It must identify itself as a placement agency in all marketing. This section does not apply to a direct-service (employer) agency; the manual should state which model the agency uses.

citations.title: License Application - evidence of liability insurance
citations.requirement: The agency must show evidence of liability insurance. The 245.30(b)(2) text confirms the cross-reference. The minimum limits were not confirmed; a secondary source says $1M per occurrence and $3M aggregate, which is unverified.

citations.title: Provisional License
citations.requirement: Provisional license valid 240 days, extendable 120 days with substantial progress. The full home services license expires one year from the end of the month the provisional license was first issued. (From the fact-checked research.)

citations.title: Adverse Licensure Actions - application not completed within 90 days
citations.requirement: An application not completed and approved within 90 days of submission may be denied (as cited by IDPH; from the research).

citations.title: Home Services Agencies Frequently Asked Questions
citations.requirement: Licensees take private pay or private insurance. Medicaid clients are served through IDoA CCP or DHS-DRS. IDPH does an initial application review within 30 days. A compliance survey takes place within 30 days of provisional license expiration. The agency needs IDPH approval before serving a new county. The agency must notify IDPH within 10 days of any change, using the Facility Information Change Form. (From the research.)

citations.cite: IDPH Guidance for Common Deficiency Findings
citations.title: Common Survey Deficiencies - annual registry verification and education
citations.requirement: Surveyors cite 245.71 (home services only) and 973.140 for training deficiencies. The guidance covers annual Health Care Worker Registry verification and annual education. Training records must show date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content and worker signature. This is survey guidance, not a rule.

citations.title: Home Services Application
citations.requirement: The application requires: complaint-resolution policy; employee health and safety policy; infection control policy; background-check process; supervisory-visit policies; employee training procedure (245.71); sample service plan; job descriptions; and proof of IDPH Registry access. A $1,500 fee by check or money order is due with the application. The form has an 'Alternate Agency Manager' line. (From the research.)

citations.cite: HFS Electronic Visit Verification; December 2025 Illinois EVV Updates
citations.title: Illinois EVV for Medicaid personal care
citations.requirement: Personal care and home health EVV data is integrated in HHAeXchange from March 2, 2026. HFS requires at least 75% quarterly EVV compliance from April 1, 2026. The state EVV solution is free to providers. (From the research.)

citations.cite: IDoA Community Care Program current rates (eff. 1/1/2026)
citations.title: CCP in-home service rate S5130
citations.requirement: CCP in-home service (S5130) is $30.80/hour statewide, or $32.57/hour with insurance. IDoA is the operating agency, and Care Coordination Units assess and refer clients. Senior HelpLine 1-800-252-8966 is for client applications. (From the research.)

citations.title: HSP maximum unit prices
citations.requirement: Homemaker (4100) $30.80/hour; personal assistant (4150) $20.00/hour; non-agency CNA (4198) $23.00/hour. HSP serves people with severe disabilities under age 60. (From the research.)

citations.cite: HFS Persons who are Elderly waiver
citations.title: Persons who are Elderly HCBS waiver
citations.requirement: HFS is the state Medicaid agency and IDoA is the operating agency for the Persons who are Elderly waiver. (From the research.)

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Agency Manager Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Agency Manager, Alternate Agency Manager and all employees
policies.purpose: To establish who holds legal authority over [AGENCY NAME], who is accountable for day-to-day operations, and how the agency is organized, so that non-medical home services are delivered safely and in compliance with the Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Licensing Act and 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is governed by a governing body that holds legal authority over the agency. The governing body maintains bylaws or the equivalent, reviews them at least annually, adopts and revises operating policies and procedures, meets to review agency operations, and keeps minutes of all meetings (245.30(a)). The governing body designates an Agency Manager to supervise the provision of services (245.30(f)(1)) and designates in writing a qualified Alternate Agency Manager to act in the manager's absence (245.40(a)). The Agency Manager carries out the duties listed in 245.40(a)(1)-(13). [AGENCY NAME] is a home services agency. It does not hold itself out as a home health agency, and the registered-nurse supervisor requirements that apply to home health agencies do not apply to this agency.

definitions.definition: The owner, board or other group that holds legal authority over [AGENCY NAME] and is responsible for its policies and operations.
The person designated by the governing body to supervise the provision of services and to manage the agency's daily operations.
The qualified person designated in writing to act when the Agency Manager is absent. This person is listed on the IDPH application.
The written document, or its equivalent, that states the agency's objectives and how the governing body operates.

procedures: The governing body documents its legal authority in the agency's formation documents, which are kept in the governance file at [ADDRESS].
The governing body adopts written bylaws or the equivalent. The bylaws state the agency's objectives.
At least once every 12 months, the governing body reviews the bylaws, revises them as needed, and records the review and any revisions in the minutes.
The governing body meets at least quarterly to review agency operations, including the quality improvement report (GOV-04), complaints, incidents and survey results.
The governing body secretary records minutes of every meeting, and the chair signs and dates them. Minutes are kept in the governance file.
The governing body adopts the operating policies and procedures in this manual and any revision to them. Each adoption is recorded in the minutes (see GOV-03).

Before the license application is filed, the governing body contacts IDPH (217-782-7412) to confirm what documents or qualifications IDPH expects for the Agency Manager, because no qualification list for home services agency managers was found in 245.30(f). The response is filed in the governance file.
The governing body designates [AGENCY MANAGER NAME] as Agency Manager in a signed written resolution that states the manager's duty to supervise the provision of services.

The governing body designates [ALTERNATE AGENCY MANAGER NAME] in writing to act in the manager's absence. This person is entered on the 'Alternate Agency Manager' line of the IDPH application (Form 445104).
The Agency Manager ensures the agency complies with the Act, 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245 and other applicable laws, and keeps a current copy of the Department's rules in the agency office.
The Agency Manager familiarizes all employees with the Act and rules during orientation and whenever the rules change, and records this in the employee's training record (PER-03).
The Agency Manager keeps agency reports, client records, personnel files and policies on file, protects them from unauthorized access, and makes them available to IDPH surveyors.

The Agency Manager maintains an organizational chart that shows lines of authority from the governing body through the manager and supervisors to the home services workers and the clients they serve. The chart is updated whenever positions change.
The Agency Manager hires staff according to written job descriptions (PER-08) and arranges orientation and in-service education (PER-03).

Supervisory functions are assigned to persons who meet the qualifications in PER-09. The agency does not employ a registered nurse supervisor to meet any home services licensing requirement unless the governing body chooses to add nursing services and obtains the appropriate license.

If the Agency Manager or Alternate Agency Manager changes, the Agency Manager notifies IDPH within 10 days on the Facility Information Change Form, as set out in GOV-02, and the governing body records the new designation in the minutes.
The governing body reviews the Agency Manager's performance at least annually (PER-08) and records the review.

responsibilities.duty: Hold legal authority; adopt and review bylaws annually; adopt and revise policies; meet and keep minutes; designate the Agency Manager and Alternate in writing.
Sign minutes and resolutions; ensure the annual bylaws review occurs.

Perform the duties in 245.40(a): ensure compliance, keep the rules and records, keep the organizational chart, hire per job descriptions, provide orientation and in-service education, and supervise services.

responsibilities.role: Alternate Agency Manager ([ALTERNATE AGENCY MANAGER NAME])
responsibilities.duty: Act in the manager's absence with the same authority and responsibility for operations.
Know and follow the Act, the rules and this manual.

documentation: Formation documents showing legal authority
Bylaws with annual review dates
Governing body minutes
Written designation of Agency Manager
Written designation of Alternate Agency Manager
Current organizational chart
Copy of the Act and 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245
IDPH response on manager documentation
Employee acknowledgment of rules orientation

policies.title: Licensure, Service Area, Insurance and Advertising Requirements
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Agency Manager, Alternate Agency Manager, and staff who handle marketing, intake or scheduling
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] holds the required IDPH license before serving any client, serves only approved counties, keeps its license and insurance current, reports changes to IDPH on time, and advertises accurately.
policies.policy: No one may open, manage, conduct or maintain a home services agency in Illinois without an IDPH license (210 ILCS 55). [AGENCY NAME] will not accept or serve a client until IDPH has issued at least a provisional Home Services Agency license. [AGENCY NAME] is a direct-service (employer) agency. It employs and directs its home services workers. It is not a home services placement agency, and the placement-agency rules in 245.214 (one-time placement fee only; no direction or supervision of the worker; 'placement agency' labeling in marketing) do not apply. The agency serves private-pay and private-insurance clients under its license. Medicaid clients are served through the IDoA Community Care Program or DHS-DRS Home Services Program (see SVC-10). The agency serves only counties approved by IDPH, keeps liability insurance in force, notifies IDPH of changes within 10 days, and does not advertise services or counties it is not licensed to provide.

definitions.definition: The initial license, valid 240 days and extendable by 120 days if the agency shows substantial progress (245.100).
An agency that employs and supervises its own workers, as opposed to a placement agency that only refers workers.
The IDPH form used to report changes such as ownership, manager, address or telephone.
The Illinois counties that IDPH has approved for the agency.

procedures: Before operating, the governing body confirms whether any exclusion in 245.20 applies. Programs that serve clients only through IDoA CCP, the DHS Office of Rehabilitation Services, or the VA are not home services agencies. [AGENCY NAME] will also serve private-pay clients, so it applies for the license.

The Agency Manager completes IDPH Form 445104 and assembles the application package. The package includes the complaint-resolution policy, employee health and safety policy, infection control policy, background-check process, supervisory-visit policies, employee training procedure, sample service plan, job descriptions, and proof of access to the IDPH Health Care Worker Registry.

The Agency Manager mails the application with the $1,500 fee by check or money order. IDPH does not accept electronic submission or electronic payment, and the fee is non-refundable. The manager keeps a copy of the full package and proof of mailing.

IDPH performs an initial review within 30 days of submission. The Agency Manager answers every IDPH deficiency request promptly, because an application that is not completed and approved within 90 days of submission may be denied (245.130(b)). The manager calendars the 90-day date on the day of mailing.
No staff member may accept, assess or begin services for any client until the provisional license is issued. Intake staff will tell inquirers that services are not yet available.

On receipt of the provisional license, the Agency Manager records its effective date, the 240-day expiration date and the date 30 days before expiration. IDPH conducts an on-site survey within 30 days of provisional license expiration. The agency is prepared for that survey (GOV-08) from its first day of operation.

If the agency needs more time to complete license requirements, the Agency Manager requests the 120-day extension from IDPH before the provisional license expires and documents the substantial progress made.

The full license expires one year from the end of the month in which the provisional license was first issued. The Agency Manager calendars the expiration date and submits the renewal application at least 60 days before expiration. The renewal fee is confirmed with IDPH before submission.
The agency displays its license in the office where clients and visitors can see it, and keeps a copy in the governance file.
Before serving any client in a county not on the agency's approved list, the Agency Manager obtains IDPH approval for that county. Intake staff accept clients only from approved counties.

The Agency Manager notifies IDPH within 10 days of any change, including ownership, Agency Manager, Alternate Agency Manager, address or telephone, using the Facility Information Change Form. A copy and proof of submission are filed.

The Agency Manager keeps evidence of liability insurance in force as required by 245.30(b)(2) and 245.90(a). The Agency Manager confirms the minimum limits required by IDPH before purchasing coverage, then carries at least those limits. The certificate is filed and the renewal date calendared 60 days ahead.

Because the agency is a direct-service employer, all marketing, the website and the service agreement identify the agency as the clients' provider and employer of its workers. No marketing may describe the agency as a placement agency or promise a one-time-fee referral service.

The Agency Manager reviews all advertising and marketing before use. Materials may show license status accurately, list only IDPH-approved counties, and describe only non-medical home services within the scope in SVC-01.
Materials may not state or imply that the agency provides nursing, medication administration or other medical services.
The Agency Manager reports to the governing body at each meeting on license, insurance and service-area status, and the minutes record the report.
IDPH contact for licensing questions: Home Services Program, 217-782-7412 (TTY 800-547-0466), DPH.COOS@illinois.gov.

responsibilities.duty: Authorize the application and renewal; ensure the license and insurance stay in force; review license status at each meeting.
Prepare and file the application, renewal and change forms; track deadlines; obtain IDPH approval for new counties; approve marketing.
Accept clients only after licensure and only from approved counties; refer others elsewhere.
Carry out these duties in the manager's absence.

documentation: Form 445104 and complete application package with proof of mailing and fee
IDPH correspondence and deficiency responses
Provisional and full license with expiration calendar
IDPH county approval letters and current service-area list
Facility Information Change Forms with proof of submission
Certificate of liability insurance
Marketing materials with manager approval dates
Governing body minutes recording license status reports

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Agency Manager and all employees
policies.purpose: To keep the agency's written policies current, approved, available to staff, and consistent with the Act and 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains written administrative policies and procedures that ensure safe and adequate care (245.30(b)(1)). The governing body adopts and revises the policies, reviews the bylaws at least annually, and records each action in the minutes (245.30(a)). The Agency Manager keeps the Department's rules on file and makes them available to employees and contracted providers (245.40(a)). Policies are version-controlled so staff and surveyors can see which version is in effect.

definitions.definition: The collection of written policies and procedures adopted by the governing body, including this document.
A record of each policy's revision date, change summary and approval date.
The master copy kept by the Agency Manager; printed copies are for reference only.

procedures: The Agency Manager keeps the master policy manual in the agency office and an electronic copy with restricted editing rights.
Each policy shows its ID, title, effective date, version number and last review date.
The governing body reviews the bylaws at least once every 12 months and revises them as needed. The minutes record the date and outcome.
The Agency Manager reviews every policy at least annually and presents the results to the governing body, which approves, revises or retires each policy and records the action in the minutes.

The Agency Manager also reviews affected policies within 30 days of any change to the Act, 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245, IDoA, HFS or DHS-DRS program rules, or after any survey finding, complaint trend or incident that shows a policy gap.
The Agency Manager maintains a version log showing each revision, who proposed it, the reason, the approval date and the date staff were informed.
The Agency Manager keeps current copies of the Act, 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245 and the Department's rules in the office, and tells employees and contracted providers where they are.

The package submitted with IDPH Form 445104 contains policies on complaints, employee health and safety, infection control, background checks, supervisory visits, training, service plan, and job descriptions. The Agency Manager keeps those policies current and consistent with what IDPH reviewed. Before changing any of them, the manager checks the change against the rules.
Approved revisions are distributed to staff within 10 days. Each employee signs an acknowledgment, which is filed in the personnel record (PER-05).
Superseded versions are marked 'superseded' and kept in the archive for at least [RETENTION PERIOD SET BY THE GOVERNING BODY, NOT LESS THAN 5 YEARS] so past practice can be shown to a surveyor.
Outdated printed copies are removed from circulation when a new version is issued.
Contracted providers receive the policies relevant to their services (GOV-07).

responsibilities.duty: Adopt and revise policies; review bylaws annually; record actions in minutes.
Maintain the controlled manual, version log and rules on file; schedule reviews; distribute revisions.
Follow the current version and sign acknowledgments.

documentation: Policy manual with version log
Governing body minutes recording policy and bylaws reviews
Staff acknowledgment forms
Archive of superseded versions
Copy of the Act and rules

policies.title: Quality Improvement Program
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Agency Manager, supervisors and all employees
policies.purpose: To evaluate the quality and safety of [AGENCY NAME]'s services each year and use the results to improve care and compliance.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written quality improvement program, as 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.240(a) requires for home services agencies. The program evaluates the agency's total program at least once a year. The agency's quality improvement program also includes the record review required by 245.240(b). Before the program is finalized, the Agency Manager reads 245.240 in full and adds any content requirement not described here. Results are reported to the governing body and recorded in its minutes.

definitions.definition: The agency's written, ongoing process for measuring its performance and acting on findings.
The annual review of all agency services, policies and operations.
A scheduled review of a sample of client records for completeness and compliance.

procedures: The Agency Manager writes the QI program and presents it to the governing body for approval. The program names a QI lead (the Agency Manager unless the governing body assigns another person).
The Agency Manager reads 245.240 in full and confirms the program meets every content requirement in that section, including record review. Gaps found are corrected before the program is adopted.
At least once a year, the QI lead evaluates the agency's total program and completes a written annual evaluation report.

The QI lead gathers these inputs: client records and service plans; supervisory-visit findings; client grievances and complaints (CR-02); incident reports and abuse, neglect or exploitation investigations (SAF-01, SAF-02, SAF-08); missed-visit data (SVC-06); EVV and timekeeping data (SVC-07); training and competency evaluation results (PER-03); and client satisfaction feedback.

The QI lead reviews a sample of active and closed client records at least [QUARTERLY] to check that each record has the content required by REC-01, including personal information, emergency notification information, agreed service plan, service contract, and documentation of services at each visit.
The QI lead identifies trends, such as repeated missed visits, late supervisory visits, recurring complaints or falls, and records them in the report.
For each finding, the QI lead writes a corrective action with the responsible person and a target date.
The Agency Manager carries out the actions and checks that each is completed on time. The QI lead re-checks the same measure at the next review to confirm the correction worked.
The Agency Manager presents the annual evaluation and any interim QI findings to the governing body, which reviews them, directs further action and records this in the minutes.
The Agency Manager updates affected policies (GOV-03) or training (PER-03) when QI findings show they are needed.
QI documents are kept confidential and, where they contain client information, protected under CR-03.

responsibilities.duty: Approve the QI program; review annual evaluation; direct corrective action.
Write and run the program; complete record reviews and the annual evaluation; track corrective actions.
Supply supervisory-visit findings and data; help carry out corrective actions.
Cooperate with record reviews and report quality concerns.

documentation: Written QI program
Record review tools and completed reviews
Annual total-program evaluation report
Corrective action log
Governing body minutes recording QI reports

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Agency Manager, billing and scheduling staff, supervisors and home services workers
federal: 42 USC 1396b(l) (Social Security Act section 1903(l): electronic visit verification for Medicaid personal care services)
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] bills only for services actually delivered and documented, follows payer rules, and gives staff a safe way to report suspected fraud or billing errors.
policies.policy: 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245 has no separate compliance-program rule, but the Agency Manager must ensure compliance with all applicable federal, State and local laws (245.40(a)). [AGENCY NAME] bills only for services that are documented in the visit record and delivered under the service plan. For clients served through the IDoA Community Care Program (CCP) or the DHS-DRS Home Services Program (HSP), the agency bills only at the program's posted rate and only for visits verified through electronic visit verification (EVV). Exclusion screening, audits and the non-retaliation reporting channel described here are controls the agency sets for itself; they are not drawn from an Illinois rule.

definitions.definition: Billing only for services that were authorized, delivered and documented, at the correct rate.
Knowingly billing or documenting for services not delivered, or falsifying a record, to obtain payment.
Electronic visit verification, a system that records the time, place, service and worker for each visit (see SVC-07).
The IDoA Community Care Program in-home service code. It is $30.80 per hour statewide, or $32.57 per hour with insurance (effective 1/1/2026).
The DHS-DRS Home Services Program homemaker service. Its maximum unit price is $30.80 per hour (updated 7/1/2026).

procedures: The governing body adopts this policy and names the Agency Manager as compliance lead. The manager reports compliance matters to the governing body at each meeting.
At hire, each employee receives this policy and signs an acknowledgment. Billing and scheduling staff receive additional training on payer rules before they handle claims or invoices.
Workers record the start time, end time and services delivered for every visit at the time of the visit (SVC-07). No worker may record or sign for services not provided.

Before any invoice or claim is issued, billing staff match it to the verified visit record and the service plan. A visit with no verified record, or with services outside the plan, is held and reviewed by the Agency Manager.
For private-pay clients, billing staff charge only the rates and terms in the signed service agreement (CR-06).

For CCP clients, billing staff bill only authorized units at the current CCP rate (S5130: $30.80 per hour, or $32.57 per hour with insurance, effective 1/1/2026) and only for EVV-verified visits. Rates are checked against the IDoA current-rates page each time IDoA publishes a change.

For HSP clients, billing staff bill only authorized units at no more than the HSP maximum unit price in effect (homemaker 4100: $30.80 per hour, per the schedule updated 7/1/2026). Rates are checked against the DHS-DRS posted schedule when it changes.

For Medicaid personal care visits, the agency uses EVV that integrates with HHAeXchange (integration begins March 2, 2026) and monitors its EVV compliance each month. HFS requires at least 75% quarterly EVV compliance from April 1, 2026. Visits with manual edits are reviewed by the Agency Manager, and the reason is documented. The agency may use the state EVV solution, which is offered at no cost to providers.

The Agency Manager audits a sample of at least [10 PERCENT OR 10 VISITS PER MONTH, WHICHEVER IS GREATER] visits monthly, comparing the EVV record, timesheet, service plan and invoice. Errors are corrected, and overbilled amounts are refunded to the client or payer promptly.

Before hiring, and at least [ANNUALLY] after, the agency screens each employee and contractor against the federal and Illinois exclusion lists as an agency-set control, in addition to the Health Care Worker Registry checks in PER-02.

Any employee who suspects fraud, a billing error or falsified records reports it to the Agency Manager, or to the governing body chair if the concern involves the manager. Reports may be made verbally or in writing and may be anonymous.
The agency prohibits retaliation against anyone who makes a good-faith report. Retaliation is grounds for discipline up to termination (PER-07).

The Agency Manager investigates every report within [10] business days, documents the findings and corrective action, and reports serious findings to the governing body. Overpayments are refunded, and the agency reports to the payer as the payer's program rules require.
The Agency Manager reports the results of audits and investigations to the governing body at least annually, and the results are used in the QI program (GOV-04).
Staff may not accept gifts, loans or money from clients, or use a client's funds, as a way to increase pay or billing (CR-04).

responsibilities.duty: Adopt this policy; receive compliance reports; handle reports involving the Agency Manager.
Run audits and exclusion screening; investigate reports; confirm rates and EVV compliance.
Bill only verified, authorized services at correct rates; hold and escalate discrepancies.
Document accurately and report suspected fraud or errors.

documentation: Signed policy acknowledgments
Monthly billing audit records
EVV compliance reports and manual-edit reviews
Rate verification records for CCP and HSP
Exclusion screening records
Compliance report log and investigation files
Governing body minutes

policies.title: Operating Hours, Office and After-Hours Access
policies.applies_to: Agency Manager, Alternate Agency Manager, office and scheduling staff, supervisors and clients
policies.purpose: To make sure clients, workers and the public can reach [AGENCY NAME] during business hours, can reach care outside those hours, and that the office protects records and meets fire-safety requirements.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains an office at [ADDRESS] with a working telephone that is staffed during business hours (245.40(a)). The office protects the confidentiality of paper and electronic records and complies with local fire-safety ordinances. The agency has a written operating-hours policy that tells clients how to access care from the agency, or from another provider, outside those hours. A supervisor is reachable by workers at all times while services are being provided.

definitions.definition: The hours the office is open and the telephone is staffed: [DAYS AND HOURS].
The telephone number that clients and workers use outside business hours: [AFTER-HOURS PHONE].
The supervisor assigned to answer the after-hours line and support workers.

procedures: The agency keeps its office at [ADDRESS]. The main telephone number is [PHONE].
The agency sets its business hours as [DAYS AND HOURS]. The governing body approves any change, and the Agency Manager updates all materials within 10 days.
During business hours, a trained staff member answers the office telephone. If the line is not answered live, the call is returned within [1] business hour.

The agency's written operating-hours policy states the business hours and what clients should do outside those hours. The Agency Manager gives it to every client at intake with the service agreement (CR-06) and explains it verbally.
Outside business hours, clients and workers call [AFTER-HOURS PHONE], which reaches the on-call supervisor. If a caller cannot get a live response, the call is returned within [30] minutes.
The Agency Manager posts a weekly on-call schedule naming the supervisor, a backup, and their telephone numbers. A supervisor is reachable by workers at all times while services are provided.
For a medical emergency, workers and clients are instructed to call 911 first and then notify the on-call supervisor (SVC-08).

If a client needs care when the agency cannot provide it, such as outside the hours in the service agreement, the on-call supervisor tells the client about other options. These include arranging coverage by another worker, contacting the client's emergency contact, or referring the client to another provider or community resource.
The on-call supervisor logs every after-hours call with the date, time, caller, issue, action taken and follow-up needed. The Agency Manager reviews the log the next business day.
The office keeps client and personnel records in locked cabinets and password-protected systems, accessible only to authorized staff (CR-03, REC-03).
The office complies with local fire-safety ordinances. The Agency Manager keeps documentation of inspections, and extinguishers, exits and any required alarms are checked at least annually.
The Agency Manager reviews this policy at least annually (GOV-03) and checks the after-hours log as part of the QI program (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Approve the operating-hours policy and office location.
Maintain the staffed office, telephone and on-call schedule; ensure record security and fire-safety compliance.
Answer the after-hours line, support workers, and log all calls.
Answer the telephone and explain the operating-hours policy to callers.
Cover these duties when the manager is absent.

documentation: Written operating-hours policy
Client acknowledgment of the operating-hours policy
Weekly on-call schedule
After-hours call log
Fire-safety inspection records
Records-security procedures

policies.title: Contracted Services and Subcontractor Agreements
policies.applies_to: All contracted or subcontracted persons and organizations that provide services to [AGENCY NAME] clients, and the Agency Manager and staff who arrange, supervise and pay for those services.
policies.purpose: To make sure that any service [AGENCY NAME] provides through a third party is covered by a written contract, is performed by qualified and screened workers, and stays under the agency's control and supervision, as the Illinois Home Services Agency rules require.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] may provide non-medical home services directly or by contract. No third party may provide services to an agency client until a written contract containing all nine required elements is signed by both parties. Contracted workers must meet the same health evaluation and background check requirements as agency employees. They must hold any license, registration or certification their role requires. They must work under the agency's supervision and follow agency policies and personnel requirements. The agency remains responsible to the client, the payer and IDPH for services delivered under a contract.

definitions.definition: A service the agency has agreed to provide to a client that is delivered by a person or organization other than an agency employee, under a written contract.
The individual, staffing entity or other business that supplies workers or services to the agency under a written contract.
The agency's authority to assign, direct, supervise, evaluate and remove the contracted worker for work performed for agency clients.
Any State professional license, registration or certification that the position requires by law or by the agency's own job description.

procedures: The Agency Manager ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) decides whether a service will be delivered by contract. Each contracted service must be on the agency's list of services offered, with a scope of work.
Before any contracted worker is assigned to a client, the Agency Manager executes a written contract with the contractor. A verbal or email-only arrangement is not accepted.

Every contract includes these nine elements: (1) a description of the services to be provided; (2) a requirement that the contractor adhere to agency policies and personnel requirements; (3) full agency control over the services; (4) a requirement that service notes be provided to the agency; (5) the charges; (6) liability and insurance, including responsibility for employment taxes and workers' compensation; (7) the term of the contract; (8) signatures of both parties; and (9) termination conditions.
The Agency Manager uses the agency's standard contract template. Any change to the nine elements is reviewed by [LEGAL COUNSEL OR REVIEWER] before signing.

Before the first assignment, Human Resources confirms for each contracted worker that the worker has completed a health evaluation equivalent to the agency's employee health evaluation. It also confirms that the worker has cleared the Health Care Worker Background Check and Registry check required of agency employees (see PER-02 and PER-04). Copies or verification records are kept in the contractor file.

For any position that requires a State professional license, Human Resources verifies with IDFPR that the license is active and keeps a copy of the verification. Verification is repeated before each license renewal date.
For any position that requires a registration or certification, Human Resources verifies it and files evidence of it.

The contractor's workers complete the agency's orientation and any task-specific competency evaluations required for the services they will perform (see PER-03 and SVC-11) before working alone with a client.

The Home Services Supervisor assigns each contracted worker to a client, includes the worker in the client's service plan, and supervises the worker the same way as an employee, including supervisory visits (see SVC-04).

Contracted workers record each visit and service in the agency's client record format. They submit service notes to the agency by the end of the same shift or as the contract specifies. The Home Services Supervisor reviews notes weekly.
The agency requires proof of the contractor's liability insurance and workers' compensation coverage before signing, and again at each renewal. The Agency Manager calendars expiration dates.

Contracted workers follow the agency's abuse, neglect and exploitation reporting, incident reporting and confidentiality policies. The Home Services Supervisor reviews these duties with each worker (see SAF-01, SAF-02 and CR-03).
The agency tells each client when a contracted worker will provide a service. The client agreement and the list of services given to the client reflect services that are contracted.

The Agency Manager reviews each contract at least annually, and before renewal, for performance, complaints, incidents and compliance with the nine required elements. The result is reported to the QI committee (see GOV-04).

If a contractor or its worker does not comply with agency policies or personnel requirements, the Agency Manager removes the worker from agency clients' care and may terminate the contract under its termination terms. The agency documents the reason.
The Agency Manager keeps a contract register that lists each contractor, service, start and end dates, required credentials, and verification dates.

responsibilities.duty: Approves and signs contracts, confirms the nine elements are present, keeps the contract register, and ends non-compliant contracts.
Verifies licenses, registrations, certifications, health evaluations and background checks for contracted workers before assignment.
Assigns, supervises and evaluates contracted workers and reviews their service notes.
Approves the use of contracted services and reviews the annual contractor performance summary.
Meets agency policies and personnel requirements, supplies qualified screened workers, provides notes and maintains insurance.

documentation: Signed written contract for each contractor, with all nine elements.
Contractor file with license, registration or certification verification, health evaluation evidence, background check and Registry results, and insurance certificates.
Orientation and competency records for contracted workers.
Contract register with start, end and renewal dates.
Service notes and supervisory visit records for contracted workers.
Annual contract review record.

policies.title: IDPH Surveys, Inspections, Complaint Investigations and Plans of Correction
policies.applies_to: The Agency Manager, the designated IDPH contact, the alternate agency manager, all supervisory staff, and all employees who may be asked questions or asked for records during an IDPH survey or investigation.
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] is ready for IDPH licensing surveys, inspections and complaint investigations. It also sets how the agency cooperates, responds to findings, and tracks every correction to completion.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] cooperates fully and courteously with IDPH. The agency names one person to receive IDPH contacts and respond the same day. It keeps records readily available for review. It runs internal mock surveys and corrects every deficiency finding with documented evidence. IDPH conducts an on-site compliance survey within 30 days of the provisional license expiring. The agency prepares for that survey well in advance and keeps records that support annual Health Care Worker Registry verification and annual education.

definitions.definition: The person named in writing by the Agency Manager to receive all IDPH calls, letters and emails and to respond the same business day.
The time-limited license issued to a new agency. A compliance survey takes place within 30 days of its expiration, before a full license is issued.
The agency's written response to survey findings that states what will be corrected, how, by whom and by what date.
An internal review of the agency's records and practices, performed using IDPH's application requirements and common-deficiency guidance as a checklist.

procedures: The Agency Manager names one IDPH contact and one back-up in writing. Their names, phone numbers and email addresses are posted in the office and given to IDPH. Any change is reported to IDPH through the Facility Information Change Form within 10 days.

The IDPH contact checks the agency's voicemail and email at least every business morning and afternoon. The IDPH contact responds to any IDPH communication the same business day, even if only to acknowledge it and give a date for the full response.
The Agency Manager keeps a current copy of the Illinois Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Licensing Act and the Department's rules in the office and makes them available to staff.

Before the survey window, the Agency Manager assigns each application-package item to an owner: complaint-resolution policy; employee health and safety policy; infection control policy; background-check process; supervisory visit policies; employee training procedure; sample service plan; job descriptions; and proof of IDPH Registry access. Each owner confirms the item is complete and current.

About 60 days before the provisional license ends, the Agency Manager and the QI lead conduct a mock survey. It samples client records, personnel files, training records, supervisory visit records, complaint and incident logs, and the policy manual. It checks that these match what the policies say.

The mock survey specifically checks the areas IDPH's common-deficiency guidance covers. Registry verification is checked for each worker, including annual re-verification. Annual education records must show the date, minutes per topic, instructor and qualifications, content covered and the worker's signature.
Findings from the mock survey are written down with an owner and a due date, and are corrected at least 14 days before the expected survey. The Agency Manager signs off on each correction.

When IDPH arrives, the first person to greet the surveyor asks for identification and notifies the IDPH contact at once. The IDPH contact or the Agency Manager meets the surveyor, escorts them, and is present for interviews unless the surveyor says otherwise.

Records requested by the surveyor are provided promptly. Staff do not alter, back-date or add to records after a survey begins. Late entries must be clearly labeled with the actual date and are made only when they correct a real omission.

Staff answer surveyor questions truthfully and only about what they know. If they do not know, they say so and refer the question to the IDPH contact. No one is told to hide records or avoid the surveyor, and no one is retaliated against for speaking with IDPH.
The IDPH contact keeps a running log of surveyor requests and documents provided, and holds a daily debrief with the Agency Manager during the survey.
At the exit conference the Agency Manager and IDPH contact take notes, ask for clarification of any finding, and ask when the written statement of findings will arrive.

When the written findings arrive, the Agency Manager reviews them within 2 business days and assigns each finding to an owner with a corrective action and due date. The plan of correction is submitted to IDPH by the date IDPH specifies.

The plan of correction states, for each finding, what will be fixed, how similar problems will be prevented, who is responsible, the completion date, and how the agency will monitor that the fix holds.

The agency keeps a copy of every IDPH finding and the correction made, with supporting evidence such as training sign-in sheets, corrected forms and revised policies. The Agency Manager checks each item as completed.
The Agency Manager follows up 30 and 90 days after correction to confirm the fix is still working. Results are reported to the QI committee (see GOV-04).

If IDPH investigates a complaint about the agency, the same process applies: the IDPH contact responds the same day, records are preserved and produced, and the Agency Manager documents the findings and any corrective action. The complainant is not retaliated against (see CR-02).

responsibilities.duty: Names the IDPH contact and back-up, leads survey readiness, signs the plan of correction and verifies corrections.
Receives IDPH communications, responds the same day, escorts surveyors and keeps the survey log.
Acts as IDPH contact and survey host when the Agency Manager or contact is unavailable.
Keeps personnel, Registry verification and training records ready for review.
Keeps client records, service plans and supervisory visit records ready for review and corrects record findings.
Runs the mock survey and tracks corrections to completion.
Cooperate with surveyors, answer truthfully, and never alter records.

documentation: Written designation of IDPH contact and back-up.
Mock survey checklist, findings and corrections.
Survey log of documents requested and provided.
IDPH statement of findings, the plan of correction, and evidence of correction.
Follow-up verification at 30 and 90 days.
Copies of all IDPH correspondence and Facility Information Change Forms submitted.

policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: All clients and their representatives, and all agency employees and contracted workers who provide or arrange services.
policies.purpose: To state the rights each [AGENCY NAME] client has, and the responsibilities that go with them, and to make sure every worker respects those rights in every visit.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] treats every client with dignity and respect. Each client has the right to independence, self-determination, privacy, choice and the exercise of their rights. No one is refused service because of a protected class under the Illinois Human Rights Act. The client or the client's representative takes part in the service plan. Clients receive, in writing, the contract terms, termination conditions and complaint contact information. For clients served through the IDoA Community Care Program or the DHS-DRS Home Services Program, the agency also honors the home and community-based settings rights that apply under the waiver.

definitions.definition: A person who receives non-medical home services from the agency under a signed agreement.
A person legally authorized to act for the client, such as an agent under a power of attorney or a guardian, or a person the client has designated.
The client's right to make choices about daily life and about the services they receive, including who provides them and when.
Rights that apply to Medicaid waiver clients under federal home and community-based services rules, such as privacy, dignity, choice, and freedom from coercion and restraint.

procedures: At intake the Intake Coordinator reviews the Client Rights and Responsibilities notice with the client and representative in plain language and in the client's preferred language, and provides it in writing (see CR-05).

The notice lists these rights: to be treated with dignity and respect; to privacy, including privacy in personal care; to independence and to make choices; to take part in developing and changing the service plan; to have a representative take part; to be free from abuse, neglect, exploitation and retaliation; to have personal property respected; to have records kept confidential; to be told of services, rates and any change in advance; to receive services without discrimination; to refuse a service; to ask for a different worker; to receive notice before services end; and to make a complaint without fear of retaliation.

The notice lists these responsibilities: to give accurate information; to tell the agency of changes in condition, medications, health care providers or address; to provide a safe home; to treat workers with respect; to follow the service plan; to give notice when cancelling a visit; and to pay as agreed.
The client or representative signs an acknowledgement that the notice was explained and received. A copy goes in the client record and a copy to the client.

The signed client agreement states the termination conditions and the contact information for concerns, complaints and questions. These are reviewed with the client when the agreement is signed (see CR-06).

The agency does not refuse or discontinue service because of a protected class under the Illinois Human Rights Act. The Intake Coordinator documents the functional, non-medical reasons when a referral is not accepted (see SVC-02).

The Home Services Supervisor includes the client and the representative in developing and updating the service plan. The plan reflects the client's own preferences for schedule, tasks and manner of care (see SVC-03).

Workers are trained on client dignity, independence, self-determination, privacy, choice and rights at orientation and every year (see PER-03). Training records show the date, topic, minutes, instructor and worker signature.
